To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The stromal asporate peroxidase of tobaco plants has been crystallized.

the stromal ascorbic acid peroxidase (APX) is a novel member of the peroxidase family, which is characterized by the presence of a conserved cysteine residue and the absence of a heme group in its active site.

the chloroplastic ascpA of tobacco plants was purified to homogeneity by ammonium sulfate precipitation, DEAE-cellulose chromatography and Sepharose CL-6B gel filtration, that the enzyme is a homodimer with subunits of 23 kDa, that the subunit is composed of 199 amino acid residues, that the subunits of the enzyme are linked by two disulfide bonds, that the sub-unit has a molecular mass of 22 500 Da,
In summary, our research is concerned with
the crystallization of chloroplastic stromal ascorbic acid peroxidase of Nicotiana tabacum L. cv. Xanthi, which was purified from the chloroplasts by the following procedure.

the study of the effects of the presence of the enzyme on the kinetics of the oxidation of ascorbic acid in aqueous solutions, and the effect of the presence of ascorbic and dehydroascorbic acid on the activity of ascorbate peroxide.
a detailed investigation of the effects of the addition of the organic solvent to the aqueous solution of the ionic liquid.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the crystal structure of chloroplastic APX is a monomeric protein with the same fold as that of cytosolic APX.
the crystallization and preliminary X- ray diffraction analysis of the chloroplastic asccorbate peroxidase from tobacco plants has been performed.
the crystal belongs to space group P2, with unit cell parameters of a = 38 A, b = 78 A, c = 99 A and a = beta = gamma = 90 degrees.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have obtained the crystal of ascorbate per oxidase (APX) of tobacco plants and determined the crystal parameters, and that we have collected the diffraction data to 1.60 A resolution from a crystal of tobacco APX.
we have successfully obtained crystals of the chloroplastic asparaginyl-tRNA synthetase (AsnRS) from Arabidopsis thaliana and that the crystals are suitable for high-resolution X-ray analysis.
the crystal structure of the chloroplastic aspartate peroxidase has been successfully determined to a high resolution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a single-crystal to single-crystal (SC2SC) approach to obtain the crystal structures of proteins in their native environment is feasible.
the crystallization of chloroplast ascorbate per oxidase was successfully achieved using polyethylene glycols.
the ascorbate peroxi- dase from the chloroplasts of tobacco plants is a homodimer in solution, but the dimer is dissociated into monomers in the crystals.
